summary.headline: Rallis Q2 FY27 revenue flat at ₹858 cr and EBITDA down 18% to ₹126 cr as deficient monsoon hit kharif demand.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was ₹858 cr versus ₹861 cr a year earlier, with 5% price growth offset by similar volume decline. EBITDA fell 18% to ₹126 cr and PAT fell 17% to ₹85 cr, driven by weak kharif liquidation after uneven rainfall and channel caution. Crop Care grew 4% but Seeds fell 31% on a 26% volume drop. H1 FY27 revenue rose 3% to ₹1,880 cr and PAT rose 6% to ₹210 cr. Management said channel inventory is not elevated for crop protection and that kharif returns and rebates are fully provided, but seed and raw material inventory is high.

segments.name: Crop Care - Domestic B2C
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹556 cr, down 1% (price +5%, volume -6%). Crop Protection ₹457 cr, down 3% on 7% volume decline; Soil & Plant Health ₹74 cr, up 22% (price +15%, volume +7%).

segments.name: Crop Care - Institutional B2B
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹232 cr, up 17% (volume +8%, price +9%). Exports ₹165 cr, up ~2.5%; CSM ₹27 cr vs ₹2 cr (PEKK rebound); Domestic B2B ₹39 cr, up 11%.

segments.name: Seeds
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹70 cr, down 31% on 26% volume decline; EBITDA nil and PAT ₹(4) cr vs ₹16 cr. Paddy and cotton placements fell on water shortage; management says seed inventory is elevated but fresh.

guidance_outlook: No numerical revenue or margin guidance given; management described the outlook as cautiously constructive and uneven recovery.
Expects next kharif season to be significantly better if monsoon normalises, though no forecast was given.
Capex: H2 FY27 to be higher than H1 (H1 under ₹20 cr); full-year capex about ₹50 cr, 'a little bit more than that'.
Expects to keep generating free cash flow for the full year as raw material purchases moderate and seed inventory normalises from March.
Seed production to slow in coming season; target to carry 150% of requirement in maize, rice and bajra.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex was below ₹20 cr; H2 to be higher to fund growth and sustenance projects.
New R&D centre in Navi Mumbai: consultants and government liaison complete, likely commissioning April 2027.
Overall capacity utilisation expected to remain broadly stable; growth via product mix and efficiencies.
Focus on capital efficiency across fixed and working capital; inventory elevated versus last year.
demand_pricing: Kharif 2026 hit by ~19% deficient rain in ~43% of India; slower liquidation and high carry-forward inventory.
Management says channel inventory is not elevated and products placed only where water availability is certain; kharif returns and provisions taken for most of the market.
Herbicide demand strong but price pressure; fungicide demand weak on low disease pressure and excess supply; insecticide and new launches grew well.
Cotton area shrank about 20-25% from peak (13 mn ha to 10-10.5 mn ha); illegal seed share estimated at 25-30%, now lower. Company says it gained share in North India cotton.
Export volumes hit by lower Pendimethalin AI demand in Europe, Chinese pricing, raw material constraints and 2-4 week supply chain delays; majority of exports to Americas.

qa_highlights.question: Are all kharif sales returns accounted for, and what is channel inventory like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said kharif returns are complete for most of the market, with provisions taken for the rest; channel inventory is only what is needed to close kharif and start rabi.

qa_highlights.question: Why did export B2B volumes decline in H1, and why did the low-cost raw material benefit not show in H1 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Export volume cuts were partly deliberate to protect margins; the low-cost inventory benefit was taken in Q1 and the weighted average benefit was lost in Q2 as prices were cut to compete.

qa_highlights.question: Why are fungicide prices not being passed on despite higher input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Low disease pressure cut demand while domestic supply and Chinese imports stayed high, so the planned price pass-through was withdrawn.

qa_highlights.question: What are the full-year capex and working capital expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex: H2 above H1, full year a little above ₹50 cr. Working capital expected to normalise from March as seed purchases fall; no red flags on receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 12-13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly freight and partly M&A-related fees for evaluated opportunities.

risks_watch: Weak rabi herbicide pricing in North India and continued fungicide price pressure.
Water availability for rabi and kharif 2027; subdued January-February rain forecast; reservoirs about 70% vs 76.6% 10-year average.
Export margins and volumes under freight, insurance and Red Sea routing pressure, plus China competition.
Elevated seed and raw material inventory and working capital; whether it normalises by year-end.
Cotton market: illegal seed share, acreage recovery, and government price cap on cotton seed.
Other expense growth (12-13%) and possible M&A-related fees.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on the quarter, attributing the weakness to rainfall and the geopolitical backdrop rather than strategy; management is confident in its portfolio and launches but gave no numerical forward guidance and was evasive on the precise sales breakup by state and seed crop.
key_quotes: Overall, EBITDA for Q2FY27 stood at ₹ 126 cr, lower by 18% compared to Q2 of the previous year.
Because of excessive supply. So as I said, our insecticide business did well.
So channel inventory, I think -- so first of all, we are not flooding the channel.
Now receivables, I think, at this point of time, we don't see any red flag. I think it's all under control.

adds.what: New R&D centre in Navi Mumbai (not productive manufacturing capacity)

growth.why: No numerical revenue or margin guidance; management is 'cautiously constructive' with growth via mix and efficiencies, utilisation broadly stable, and only an R&D centre (not manufacturing capacity) due April 2027, so backing is vague.
